On The Verge Of Non Procrastination

Sep 19, 2006 • Janice Cotcher

I like to think of it less as work and more as not-procrastinating.
I am in for a very busy week. Last night I had to shop for science lab supplies and write two tests. Tonight I am going out for supper and marking 3 tests. Wednesday I have a meeting with the company that is producing the school yearbook. Thursday I have to get class averages ready for the “Meet the Teacher” night on Friday. Friday, after being at school from 8 am - 8pm, I am driving an hour out of town to a friends house for the evening. I get exhausted just thinking about my schedule (of course this is in addition to all of my lesson planning). No wonder I never get any house work done.

Despite an incident in my class where a student got himself suspended for 3 days, it has been a pretty good week. I would love to talk about the situation but all I can really say is he threw a temper tantrum because he was expected to work on his assignment. I know, I am so unreasonable.

The restaurant I am going to this evening is closer to the school than home. I figure this would be a good time to organize the science lab (I’ve been procrastinating from it for 3 weeks).
